proposal.description: The CPLD's trip drive latch_out is released once the debounced SCR read-back shows the latch set, as if the self-holding SCR needed the drive only until it fired, instead of following strike_counter's set-only latch_assert
proposal.reason: After a strike latch, latch_out at the port drops about 1 ms after latch_stat reads back high, where it should stay high until reset. Every consumer of latch_assert (supervisor, fault_cause, fault_LED) then sees it clear while the SCR stays set, so the strike latch looks like an external one.

proposal.description: fault_cause's clear-on-read also fires on spi_abort, as if any transaction that ended unvalidated also closed the fault-log read window, so a failed write wipes the fault record and its start time
proposal.reason: Suppose fault causes have been logged and the host then sends a write that is aborted (bad CRC, wrong length or timeout). A later SPI read of FAULT_CAUSE and FTIME returns zero instead of the logged causes and episode-start timestamp.

proposal.description: reg_file's read snapshot of the timestamp is retaken after every read data byte clocked out instead of only on the first data byte of the read
proposal.reason: In a burst read of TIME_0..TIME_2, the bytes come from different instants. If a millisecond tick (in particular a carry from byte 0 into byte 1 or 2) lands mid-transaction, the host gets a torn timestamp. The design should return one coherent value frozen at the start of the transaction.
